messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — noticed a spike of objects in backups-bucket that lack KMS metadata. Appears backup-agent v2.4.1 started PUTting with SSE=S3 (AES256) instead of SSE=aws:kms. Not sure if it's agent config or policy drift.
Anita: yikes. Any logs?
Jordan: pasted a CloudTrail PutObject entry from 2026-03-16 14:02 UTC:
```
{ eventName: "PutObject", userIdentity: { principalId: "svc-backup-agent" }, requestParameters: { bucketName: "backups-bucket", key: "tenant42/snap-20260316.tar.gz" }, additionalEventData: { "x-amz-server-side-encryption": "AES256" } }
```
Jordan: note: no x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id present.
Sasha: possible causes: agent defaults changed (library bump), or IAM role lost kms:Encrypt permission and fell back to AES256. We should check IAM policy and agent release notes.
Leo: quick check — looked at recent terraform plan for backup-agent role: last change 2026-03-15 by infra-deploy user. It removed explicit kms:Encrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111:key/abcd because of a refactor. That would cause PutObject to succeed without KMS if bucket policy allows SSE-S3.
Anita: timeline? how many objects? impact?
Jordan: ~120 objects in the last 2 hours, all tenant-scoped snapshots across 3 prefixes. Size ~600GB total. No restore requests observed yet.
Anita: immediate steps: 1) stop agent writes, 2) block svc-backup-agent PutObject to backups-bucket (temp deny), 3) create detection rule to alert on PutObject events with SSE!=aws:kms, 4) start re-encryption job for affected keys.
Sasha: for step 2 we can attach an inline deny to the role or update bucket policy to deny PutObject unless x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id is present. Which is less blasty?
Leo: inline deny on role is fastest. I'll push a constrained deny that only affects the current role arn:aws:iam::111111:role/svc-backup-agent and holds for 10m while we coordinate.
encops-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.example/runbooks/encryptops-reencrypt. Suggests using copy + metadata-replace with SSE-KMS.
Sasha: re-encrypt approach (one-off):
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://backups-bucket/tenant42/snap-20260316.tar.gz /tmp/snap && 
aws s3 cp /tmp/snap s3://backups-bucket/tenant42/snap-20260316.tar.gz --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111:key/abcd
```
Sasha: or server-side copy with aws s3api copy-object specifying --server-side-encryption aws:kms and --ssekms-key-id, which avoids download. We'll run in parallel with rate-limit.
Anita: add CloudTrail detection: alert when PutObject.resource like backups-bucket AND additionalEventData.x-amz-server-side-encryption != aws:kms for any principal within service account pool. Use SIEM rule id ENC-DR-004.
Jordan: agree. Also request: add kmsKeyId to our backup-agent structured logs (agent should log sse header and kms key if set). Right now logs only show an sse boolean.
Leo: we'll require that in the agent release gating. Patch: backup-agent: add header capture + unit test; CI integration test against s3mock to assert metadata header present.
Sasha: RBAC follow-ups: 1) restore explicit kms:Encrypt on role with condition aws:SourceAccount and resource key ARN, 2) reduce wide kms grants (we currently have wildcard on several keys), 3) create ephemeral KMS grant with limited TTL for long-running copy jobs.
Anita: vulnerability triage note: this is data confidentiality risk for tenants. Legal & compliance notified. We need to produce timeline and affected tenant list for incident report. Jordan can you run listing and capture object ARNs and sizes?
Jordan: on it. I'll export to s3://ops-temp/encops/1865432100-affected-list.csv and share a presigned link.
deploy-bot: @infra-deploy requested terraform change: apply denied by user lock because manual emergency update advised.
Leo: pushed the inline deny to role, effect should be immediate. Monitor for agent errors.
Jordan: saw error spikes in agent logs referencing AccessDenied for PutObject 30s after deny. Good.
Sasha: running re-encrypt dry run on a small set (5 objects) using server-side copy. Command looks good, testing throughput.
Anita: for medium-term: require backup agents to sign requests with header x-rw-kms-key-id or enforce bucket policy requiring server-side kms and forbid SSE-S3. Also add CloudTrail guardrails and an automated periodic S3 metadata scan to detect non-KMS objects.
Leo: I'll schedule an infra postmortem RFC: root cause was terraform refactor which removed explicit KMS permission; change review missed security impact. Include checklist: policy diff review, smoke test of encryption, CI gate.
Jordan: export ready: s3://ops-temp/encops/1865432100-affected-list.csv (presigned sent to security pager duty).
Anita: ok team — prioritize tenant comms draft in incident thread, mitigation in progress. Thanks. :lock:
summary: Backup agent started writing objects encrypted with SSE-S3 instead of SSE-KMS after IAM change; team applied inline deny, running re-encrypt, and planned detection + RBAC fixes.
